_note: P2-01 defect corpus for question.validate() (P2-02). AUTHORED BEFORE THE VALIDATOR,
deliberately: a corpus written afterwards describes the implementation instead of
testing it. Same rule that made routing_golden.json find substring matching.
THIS IS A DEFECT CORPUS, NOT A CORPUS OF GOOD QUESTIONS. Routing has one correct
answer per resume; a question does not. What IS decidable is whether a given
question carries a given defect, so entries label defects and the validator is
measured on precision and recall against those labels.
`accept` entries are 61% of the corpus ON PURPOSE. A validator that rejects
everything scores 100% recall, so M6c (accept-rate on good questions) is what
stops that, and it needs a substantial accept population to mean anything.
`naive_reject_risk` names the rule a naive implementation would wrongly fire on an
accept entry. Those entries are the whole point of the corpus: each rule has at
least two, and they are where the rule's real boundary is decided.
INVARIANT: every reject entry carries primary_rule, and primary_rule is present in
rules[]. Prevents attribution drift inside the corpus itself.
If an entry here is wrong, FIX THE ENTRY and record it in the ledger — never fix it
by loosening a validator rule until it passes.
No entry may be rejected for fluency, grammar, spelling, register or politeness.
The Hinglish entries are the test of that (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
TWO FINDINGS FROM AUTHORING, both encoded as entries rather than prose:
q63 — a valid T1 transfer probe names TWO fact targets by construction (the
method's metric and the target claim's), so R3 must NOT be evaluated on
TRANSFER. R6 already constrains which second subject is permitted.
q60 — the RENDERED fallback quotes the claim including its figures, so it fails
R1 by construction. That is the evidence for runtime bypassing the
validator; it is not a defect to fix in question.py.

rule_2_threshold.metric: content-word Jaccard over a MINIMAL stopword list
rule_2_threshold.finding: AGGRESSIVE stopword removal DESTROYS this signal. Stripping the interrogative words (what/did/you/how/about/do) collapsed the duplicate band to 0.167-0.455 and the distinct band to 0.000-0.250 — an overlap of -0.083, i.e. no separating threshold exists. The interrogative frame IS the duplication signal: 'what did you decide to do about X' repeated with a different X is the defect. A minimal stopword list separates at +0.169 (distinct ceiling 0.231, duplicate floor 0.400), and 0.37 is the midpoint of the usable gap above the highest BORDERLINE pair (0.333). Measured, not guessed — the same discipline that derived MARGIN_FLOOR from the 0.397/0.321 band.
